cvEn:
Ori Gerlitz, son of Shira and Motti, was born on 1 Tishri 5765 (16 September 2004) in Beersheba. He was the brother of Yahel and Anani.

Ori grew up in Beersheba until the age of two, when his family moved to San Diego in the United States. Five years later the family moved to Melbourne, Australia. The family returned to Israel when Ori was ten.

After returning to Israel, the family settled in the community of Metar in the Negev. Ori studied at the local elementary school and then at the "Metarim Branko Weiss" high school. He completed his studies with distinction in the physics and computer science track.

Ori was a mischievous and full-of-life boy who loved sports and computer games. He was a devoted, loyal friend, beloved by his close friends. He was a talented guitar player. He loved dogs very much and enjoyed hiking with his friends and family.

Ori, the middle of three siblings, had a special bond with his older brother and his younger sister. He was also a much-loved nephew and cousin.

From a very young age he loved the sea and the sand. He would run wild on the sand and go into the sea whenever he had the chance, in every season of the year. Having grown up on the sands of San Diego and Australia, the water and the sand were his place, even in the middle of winter. Whenever he could, he went to the sea, and within a second, even with his clothes on, he was among the waves.

Ori, with his golden curls, was full of light and love, with an inner calm and a strength that influenced those around him. He would make those close to him laugh with his special and witty humor.

The qualities that characterized Ori most of all were his modesty, his inner peace and his inner tranquility. He found it hard to bear injustice, was sensitive to the distress of others, and acted according to the saying "always be good to one another." Ori always saw the person standing before him, regardless of the background they came from, and always chose to see the good in every person.

On 22 March 2023 he enlisted in the IDF and served as a combat soldier in the "Kfir" Brigade, "Shimshon" Battalion. From a young age, as the grandson of Holocaust survivors, he dreamed of being a fighter and defending the country. He completed basic training and the training course very successfully, and at a very early stage his commanders noted his high abilities and saw him as a natural candidate for command.

On Shabbat, 22 Tishri 5784, Simchat Torah, 7 October 2023, at half past six in the morning, the Hamas terror organization launched a surprise attack on Israel. Under cover of massive rocket and missile fire from the Gaza Strip into wide areas of the country, thousands of terrorists infiltrated by land, sea and air, and began a murderous assault on the communities of the Gaza envelope and on Sderot, Ofakim and Netivot, at the Supernova music festival near Kibbutz Re'im and Nir Oz, on IDF bases and on travelers on the roads in the area. The terrorists murdered some eight hundred civilians in their homes and in their cars, after committing grave atrocities against them. They abducted hundreds of Israelis into the Gaza Strip, and destroyed, looted and set fire to homes and property. Hundreds of soldiers, police officers, security personnel and members of the local emergency squads fell in battle. That morning, a war began.

Ori, the son of a father from Kibbutz Nahal Oz, whose classmates and friends from the envelope were murdered and abducted that same Shabbat, was deeply influenced by his parents' struggle on behalf of the survivors and the hostages. This greatly influenced his wish to take an active part in bringing the hostages home.

Shortly before completing his combat training, the war broke out, and Ori was on operational activity in Judea and Samaria. He later moved with his battalion to the northern border. He also attended a combat medic course and afterward a squad commander course, during which he took part in fighting in the Gaza Strip.

Upon completing the squad commander course, Ori was assigned as commander of a recruit platoon in the Armored Corps' training unit. During this period, he showed in his role the ability to reach and influence his subordinates through his quiet and patient way, which was also expressed in his receipt of a commendation.

His high abilities and his strong desire to make a difference led him to continue on the command track and to attend an officers' course, with the understanding that through command and officer service he could lead his soldiers to believe in themselves and become good people and high-quality soldiers. After completing the course he returned to his battalion and was appointed platoon commander. Before taking up the role, he wrote in his notebook what he wished to say to his soldiers and staff: "Our mission is to bring every one of our soldiers back healthy and whole… you are, to me, my little brothers, my whole world is to bring you back safely." These words express the deep sense of responsibility Ori felt, a responsibility that also showed in his care for his soldiers beyond the army and in his commitment to staying in constant contact with their parents. As a commander, he influenced his soldiers and subordinates in his own special way and with his big heart.

On Saturday, 23 August 2025, during an operational activity in the Khan Younis area, an explosive device detonated and Ori was killed on the spot.

Second Lieutenant Ori Gerlitz fell in battle on 29 Av 5785 (23 August 2025). He was twenty years old. He was laid to rest in the military plot at the cemetery in Metar. He is survived by his parents, a brother and a sister.

After his fall he was promoted to the rank of Lieutenant.

In his memory, a sticker was produced with the sentence: "When he stood out, it was quietly and modestly; when he led, it was from the heart."

In his memory, an Instagram page was set up, "remember_ori_gerlitz".
